# Ke (Mark) Ma

## Reading the high-redshift Universe through simulated spectra, power spectra and statistical inference.

I am an astrophysicist working with **Prof. James S. Bolton** on the Lyman-α forest and the intergalactic medium. My research connects physical modelling, survey-forward simulations and uncertainty-aware inference to ask what future observations can reveal about cosmic reionization and metal enrichment.

## From simulated light to physical constraints

My work treats the Lyα forest not as a single observable, but as a chain: from the physics of the intergalactic medium, through simulated spectra and survey effects, to statistical measurements and parameter constraints.
:::

::: {.featured-research}
::: {.featured-copy}
::: {.research-status}
Latest · Lead-author preprint
:::

### Can WEAVE-QSO detect relics of patchy reionization?

I developed a forecast workflow for the one-dimensional Lyα forest power spectrum at $z \geq 4$. Using Sherwood-Relics simulations and WEAVE-QSO-like mock spectra, the analysis propagates survey statistics, instrumental effects and astrophysical contaminants into a covariance-aware Bayesian forecast.

The adopted survey model predicts that the large-scale imprint of patchy hydrogen reionization should be detectable at approximately **4.5σ**.

[Read arXiv:2608.13153 →](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.13153){target="_blank" rel="noopener"}
:::

### Survey-forward modelling

Mock QSO spectra, instrumental resolution, noise, continuum uncertainty, metal contamination and high-column-density absorbers are carried into the same forecast framework.

**Methods:** Python · simulation-derived spectra · covariance · MCMC
:::

::: {.research-card}
::: {.card-number}
02
:::

### Precision Lyα forest systematics

I derived and validated a four-parameter model for correlated Si III absorption in the Lyα forest power spectrum across **375** simulation variants.

**Outcome:** first-author paper published in *MNRAS*
:::

::: {.research-card}
::: {.card-number}
03
:::

### IGM metal enrichment

My current work combines Si III power-spectrum signatures with Si IV absorber statistics to constrain silicon abundance, its density dependence and UV-background assumptions.

**Status:** ongoing PhD research
:::

## A path across theory, observations and inference
:::

::: {.profile-layout}
::: {.profile-statement}
I trained in theoretical physics at **University College London**, moved into observational astronomy as a research assistant at **Tsinghua University**, and now work at the intersection of simulations and spectra during my PhD at **Nottingham**.

That route has made crossing methodological boundaries a defining part of how I work: deriving a model, implementing the numerical analysis, testing it against simulations or data, and turning the result into a clear scientific argument.

::: {.profile-note}
**Upcoming:** accepted contributed talk at COSMO-26, Leiden, August 2026.
:::

I welcome conversations around the Lyα forest, high-redshift IGM physics, spectroscopic-survey forecasting, simulation-based inference, and the broader use of quantitative modelling to extract reliable structure from complex data.
